Send a gift

Send Lightning directly to ecashcard@islandbitcoin.com. You can also use the BOLT12 offer below.

Checking your notes with the federation

Notes from any federation work, and they carry their own amount. In your Fedimint wallet, send eCash, then copy the notes it gives you.

Amount in sats

Cashu eCash from any mint. Your wallet pays a request on the next step, or you paste a token.

On-chain fees make small gifts costly. Lightning suits amounts under 100,000 sats.

Gifts go directly to the maintainers, toward work on Cashu Card. They buy no goods, services, or equity, and they are not tax deductible.

Grants and larger gifts

Foundations and companies that want to fund a specific piece of work, such as an independent security review, can write to us. We send a one-page scope with the deliverable, the reviewer or vendor, the timeline, and what gets published at the end. Reviews and test reports funded this way are published in full in the repository.

Write to hello@cashucard.org

The work so far was carried by grants from The Reynolds Foundation and the Human Rights Foundation under Project Island Resilience, and by Flash and Island Bitcoin.

Other ways to help

Gifts pay for time on the work. Scrutiny, code, and real use in the field help just as much.

  • Break it Audit the applet, the host code, and the draft NUT, and report what you find to security@cashucard.org.
  • Build on it Add card support to your wallet or till. The developer page has the protocol, the simulator, and the test vectors.
  • Issue cards Run cards on your own mint with the install guide and an operator account, load small amounts, and tell us what fails.
  • Talk about it Questions and ideas go in GitHub Discussions.
